A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMOA-RAG, with matching methods, equations and retained experiments. The material is readable and supports comparison, including v2 Appendices A-I; v1 ends with references and has no appendix.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original QA experiments, baseline comparisons, component ablations, configuration studies and out-of-domain evaluation in Tables 3-6.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices E, F and I report original QA results, including retained experiments, additional retriever comparisons and a worked inference case.

M1.justification: Both versions use three trainable agents, a fixed retriever, SFT initialization and parameter-sharing MAPPO with answer F1, agent penalties and KL regularization. The additional prompts and sharing rationale document the existing procedure; they do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both use HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA and AmbigQA with Wikipedia passages, including HotpotQA-to-AmbigQA transfer. The added BGE/E5 experiments vary the retrieval model within the existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: RAG-DDR, previously discussed only as related work, becomes an evaluated baseline in v2 Table 1 and the new Table 7. The original main-comparison baselines and out-of-domain comparator set are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a testing protocol that evaluates Contriever-trained models using BGE and E5 retrievers. The original Llama-3-8B-Instruct backbone, ten-document retrieval setting, accuracy/EM/F1 metrics and reported training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds transfer tests across two alternative retrievers on all three datasets. Appendix I adds a detailed MAPPO-versus-SFT case tracing query decomposition, retrieved evidence, document selection and answer correctness. These substantially extend the supplementary analysis; the original module ablations, configuration studies and out-of-domain experiment are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or statistical significance tests. The added comparisons continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds RAG-DDR scores, full BGE/E5 comparisons and case-study outcomes while retaining the original numerical benchmark and out-of-domain results. Adding RAG-DDR reduces the reported AmbigQA accuracy margin from 2.84 to 2.60 points. The new results include exceptions to superiority: with BGE, MMOA-RAG achieves 45.47 EM on 2WikiMultihopQA versus RetRobust's 45.57. These are additional settings, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The cooperative-agent definitions, reward equations, SFT objective, PPO losses and GAE formulation are unchanged. The SFT equation moves to Appendix B and equations are renumbered; no new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims that cooperative multi-agent optimization aligns RAG modules, improves QA performance and applies across pipeline configurations. The revised contribution list explicitly includes the already-present fixed retriever without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5 and Appendices G-H add discussion of training overhead, inference cost, possible parameter-sharing instability with more agents, and future dynamic workflows and cost-aware rewards. Appendix I interprets an SFT failure through inadequate module coordination. The interpretations of the original quantitative experiments remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 newly supplies complete query-rewriter and generator prompts in Tables 3 and 5. The selector prompt, SFT data-construction procedure, training pseudocode, hyperparameters and code-access information were already present in v1 and are principally relocated.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of Search-r1, R1-Searcher and MAO-ARAG, plus references supporting the added retrievers and MARL discussion. The earlier related-work coverage and central research positioning remain, with detailed descriptions moved to Appendix A.

P1.justification: The document is extensively reorganized: preliminary material is merged into Method, the training section is restructured, and detailed related work, SFT construction, pseudocode, implementation settings and out-of-domain evaluation move into appendices. The main narrative is condensed and new discussion and case-study appendices are introduced.

P2.justification: The two-column ACM layout becomes a single-column NeurIPS layout. Figure 1 is redrawn, v1 Table 4 becomes the three-panel ablation Figure 2 with rounded labels, and v2 adds retriever results, prompt tables and boxed inference traces. Several existing displays move into appendices.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through the RAG-DDR comparison and transfer tests across retrievers, and improves reproducibility with previously missing agent prompts and a traceable case study. These address specific evidence and documentation gaps. The gain remains limited because small performance margins lack uncertainty estimates and the added cost and scalability discussion has no measured validation.
